tldr: Blossom OS went from a static HTML mockup to a real Next.js app running locally with all 5 views, plus a founder team-briefing card.
Blossom's profile gained three governance sections: Purpose of Blossom OS, the Self-Update & File Maintenance Protocol, and Ian named as boss with final authority.
Claude (the runtime) was set up to know Blossom and connect Ian to her on request; this Mac is now treated as Blossom's own device.

briefs.body: First operational day on the new Mac. Focus: get the device set up as Blossom's home, validate API access, and convert the Blossom OS mockup into a running app. No external deadlines.

decisions.decision: Use Next.js 16 (current) instead of the brief's Next.js 14
decisions.outcome: Adopted — 14 won't run cleanly on Node 26; App Router + Tailwind structure unchanged

decisions.decision: Preserve the mockup's exact CSS as the design system rather than rewriting it in Tailwind
decisions.outcome: Adopted — faithful, fastest, honors 'make it real, don't redesign'

decisions.decision: Run Blossom on the hosted Claude platform now, keep building the custom OS in parallel; revisit local once open models catch up
decisions.outcome: Adopted as the working plan; architecture kept model-agnostic

decisions.decision: Ian is Blossom's boss with final authority; all plans are provisional

eod: Day 1 of operation. The Mac is now Blossom's home — toolchain, Claude Code, API key, and repo all in place. Blossom OS crossed from mockup to a real, running Next.js app with every view navigable locally, and the dashboard now opens with a team briefing for Ian. Blossom's charter matured: she has a stated purpose (cumulative, portable learning), a sustainable self-maintenance protocol, and a clear chain of command — Ian decides, everything else is provisional. Open for next session: rotate the exposed key when the Business account exists, decide Meadow's profile, and wire the live Claude API so the chat becomes really her.
